content.title: What a real-estate lawyer in Israel actually does for you
content.body: If someone gave you our name, you are probably asking a fair question: what exactly does a lawyer do here, and is it worth it? Here is a straight answer. We start with the title, checking the Tabu or Israel Land Authority for liens or third-party rights. We read and negotiate the contract. We coordinate with everyone involved, map the taxes and fees (mas rechisha, registration), and see final registration through to your name.
content.cta: Booking link in first comment: https://calendly.com/y-epsteinlaw/
content.note: Link goes in the first comment, not the post body.

content.title: Buying from abroad: how we make it work remotely
content.body: You found the apartment. You are three time zones away. Now what? A power of attorney (ייפוי כוח) means you do not have to fly in to sign every document. Documents move securely, communication is planned across time zones, and when closing day comes, we handle it on your behalf.
content.cta: Book a free introductory call. We work across time zones. https://calendly.com/y-epsteinlaw/
content.note: Confirm whether a named secure portal/courier is used before publishing.

content.title: 5 questions to ask before you sign in Israel
content.body: 1. Who has actually checked the title? 2. What exactly is in the contract, and what is missing? 3. Who is paying which taxes and fees, and have they been calculated? 4. What happens if the other side misses a deadline? 5. Is your lawyer representing you, or just the deal?
content.cta: Ready to talk through your deal? Book a free introductory call. https://calendly.com/y-epsteinlaw/
